label: <DEL> step, when first two original tokens are from {z,s,p,1,l,a,k,q,b,n}
explanation: Delimiter-step unit: 93% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step (t == L, where the model emits original token 0), but it fires on only about 11% of <DEL> steps. Whether it fires depends on the sequence content. It is strongly enriched when the first original token (the one being output, out_tok) and the second (next_out) come from a favored set {z,s,p,1,l,a,k,q,b,n}; requiring both gives dev F1 0.58 (P 0.62, R 0.54). Rate also rises with L (3.9-4.6x lift at t=8,9) and with the number of favored tokens seen. The remaining ~6% of mass is weak firing in the last few original-phase steps of long sequences, on first occurrences of tokens like e/t/u/i. It almost never fires in the copy phase (t > L) or at t < 3. The content dependence looks graded rather than a clean token rule, so precision and recall stay incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: z, s, p, 1; copy phase: l, z, 1, q; input phase: ) and the second original token (most: 1, l, n, a, q, s; least: 3, u, e, t); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, t=7, t=5.
